transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been really stressed about something with my dad’s lab results. I know it probably sounds like I’m making it bigger than it is, and I don’t want to come across the wrong way, but for about the past year I’ve been trying to figure out why parts of his chart don’t match what I saw.

People keep telling me the numbers are fine—doctors, my family—but I just… I know something isn’t right. It feels like someone in the clinic system is changing things or holding certain results back, and I’ve been trying to prove it. It’s been wearing me down, honestly.
Have you ever felt like others are intentionally trying to hide medical information about your father from you, even when they tell you the results are normal?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to sound accusatory or like I’m being unreasonable. But yes, that’s kind of what it feels like.

For about a year I’ve been trying to prove that something in the clinic system isn’t right—like parts of my dad’s lab results are being changed, or maybe some results are being held back. Everyone keeps telling me the numbers are normal, and I know they probably think they’re reassuring me, but the chart just doesn’t match what I saw. I can’t really let it go, and it’s been wearing me down.
Have you ever had any other experiences where you believed something strongly that others didn’t agree with, even when they told you there was no evidence to support it?

Not really other things… or at least, nothing that feels separate from this. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m always insisting I’m right or anything.

It’s mostly been this thing with my dad’s labs. For the past year I’ve just felt like I have to prove that something in the clinic system is off—like someone changed part of the results or didn’t release everything. And I know doctors and my family keep saying the numbers are fine, so maybe I’m not explaining it well, but the chart doesn’t match what I saw. I can’t shake that, and it’s been really wearing me down.
Have you ever had a time when you experienced things like hearing voices or believing something strongly that others didn’t agree with, even when there was no clear reason for it?

I haven’t heard voices or anything like that, no. Um… the main thing is what I’ve been trying to explain about my dad’s labs.

I know people keep telling me there’s no reason to think anything was changed, and I’m trying to be fair about that, but for the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing things or holding back parts of his results. The chart just doesn’t match what I saw. Doctors and my family keep saying the numbers are fine, but I know something is off, and… I know that probably sounds intense. It’s just been really wearing me down.

Have you ever had a strong belief that something was definitely true, even when there was clear evidence showing it wasn’t, and no matter how much others tried to show you otherwise, you just couldn’t let go of that belief?

I guess… yes, if I’m being honest. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m refusing to listen to people, because I do hear what they’re saying.

But I’m here because for about the past year, I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. Doctors and my family keep telling me the numbers are fine, and I know they’re probably trying to help, but I just… I know the chart doesn’t match what I saw.

I’ve tried to let it go, and I know maybe that’s what I’m supposed to say, but I can’t. It keeps bothering me, and it’s really wearing me down.
